intro.label: Careers
intro.body: A small team building high-speed UAV systems.

roles.title: Flight Software Engineer
roles.summary: Own onboard software, control, and simulation for high-speed UAV systems, from the lab to first flight.
do: Design and ship flight software for high-speed unmanned aircraft.
Build and maintain the simulation environment used to test software before it flies.
Bring up onboard computers, sensors, and radios on the bench and on the vehicle.
Debug issues across software and hardware with a small, hands-on team.
Write clear, testable code and keep the vehicle flying as the airframe and propulsion evolve.
lookingFor: Strong programming ability in C/C++ and/or Python, with comfort on Linux.
A grounding in control, embedded systems, or robotics, from coursework or shipped projects.
Experience debugging real systems, not only simulation.
Willingness to work on-site with hardware, not only remotely from a laptop.
preferred: Flight-control, autopilot, or UAV software you have actually run on a vehicle.
Familiarity with sensors, radio links, or real-time software.
A degree in computer science, aerospace, electrical, or a related field, or equivalent work.
roles.why: Direct work with the founding team on the software that flies the aircraft. Small team, high ownership, and a short path from code to the runway.

roles.title: Aerospace Engineer
roles.summary: Design, analyse, and help build the airframe: structures, aerodynamics, and the path from CAD to composite parts.
do: Own airframe design and analysis for a high-speed unmanned aircraft.
Run structural and aerodynamic analysis and turn results into hardware decisions.
Work with in-house manufacturing on composite parts, fit, and assembly.
Support ground and flight test as the vehicle comes together.
Keep drawings, models, and test notes in a state others can actually use.
lookingFor: A grounding in aircraft structures, aerodynamics, or composite design.
Comfort in CAD and in at least one analysis tool used for structures or flow.
Willingness to move between the screen and the shop floor.
Clear written communication. Short notes that a teammate can act on.
preferred: Hands-on composite, prototyping, or UAV airframe work.
A degree in aerospace, mechanical, or a related field, or equivalent work.
Experience taking a part from model to a vehicle that was actually built.
roles.why: End-to-end airframe work on a high-speed UAV, sitting with software and manufacturing rather than throwing drawings over a wall.
